name: 80K Hours Upskilling Resources
current_details: A curated collection of 67 resources for upskilling in technical AI safety research, compiled by 80,000 Hours in consultation with their advisors. Covers field overviews (AISafety.com, Anthropic's recommended research agendas, Redwood's control work), technical courses (ARENA, BlueDot Impact, Karpathy's Zero to Hero, Jacob Hilton's Deep Learning Curriculum), project ideas and open problems in evals and mech interp, advice from researchers like Neel Nanda, Ethan Perez and Richard Ngo, fellowships (Anthropic AI Safety Fellowship, MATS, Constellation Astra, LASR Labs, SPAR, Pivotal, ARENA Cambridge, ERA, CHAI, Global AI Safety Fellowship), and profiles of key technical AI safety organisations. Written by Matt Beard, first published June 4th, 2025 and last updated September 15th, 2025.

name: 80K Hours AI Safety Career Review
current_details: A comprehensive 80,000 Hours career review (last updated August 2024) on AI safety technical research, covering two main paths: empirical AI safety — open to strong software engineers who can apply for research contributor roles immediately, even without an ML background — and theoretical AI safety, suited to those with very strong maths/theoretical CS backgrounds or the ability to get into a top 10 ML PhD program. It details why the work is high impact, downsides and risk of harm, earnings, how to predict personal fit, learning resources, whether to do a PhD, job application strategies, and key organisations. It is a permanent resource page with no application deadline, linked to 80,000 Hours' job board and free 1-on-1 advising.

name: AISafety.com Events & Training
current_deadline: Updated continuously — next listed deadline 25 Sep 2026
current_details: AISafety.com maintains a continuously updated directory of 99 AI safety training programs — fellowships, bootcamps, and courses, online and in person — alongside 32 events, plus job, funding, and community listings. It currently lists 45 upcoming training programs, filterable by type, focus (technical/governance/general), entry bar, stipend, length, and location, with durations from 4 days to 1 year. Open applications include the GEAR alignment course, Effective Thesis Accelerator, IAPS AI Policy Fellowship (Spring 2027), LawAI fellowships, Iliad Fellowship, AI Security Bootcamp London, and the Anthropic AI Safety Fellows Program (Jan 2027).

structured.stipend: Varies — many programs include stipends or cover expenses
structured.location: Online & worldwide (Berkeley, London, Washington D.C., Lisbon, Lyon, Singapore)

name: AISafety.com Self-Study
current_details: A curated directory of 28 self-study curricula and reading lists for learning AI safety independently. Entries range from general introductions (BlueDot Impact's Future of AI and Intro to Transformative AI, AI Risk Fundamentals, DeepMind's 75-minute AGI Safety Short Course, AI Safety Atlas, AISES) to technical alignment training (ARENA, Introduction to ML Safety, Agent Foundations, Iliad Intensive, Harvard's CS 2881, UChicago XLab AI Security Guide) and governance/strategy material (ENAIS Deep Dive, AGI Strategy, MATS strategy curriculum, Economics of Transformative AI). It functions as a permanently maintained reference hub with no application process, alongside AISafety.com's other directories of jobs, funding, events and communities.

name: Apart Research Hackathons
current_details: Apart Research runs monthly online research sprints (hackathons) open to everyone worldwide, plus two fellowship tracks: the Apart Fellowship, which develops hackathon ideas into published research, and Partnered Fellowships, where participants apply to existing project proposals with mentorship from leading researchers. Its research focuses on manipulation and dark patterns in frontier AI systems, in collaboration with the EU AI Office and AI providers. Programs have engaged 8,000+ participants from 26 nationalities across 50+ sprints, with the top 2% joining fellowships that have published at NeurIPS, ICLR, ACL, and EMNLP.

name: BlueDot Impact
current_details: BlueDot Impact is a non-profit AI safety talent accelerator based in London and San Francisco, offering free online courses, grants for career transitions, and intensive in-person programs. Since 2022 they've trained 10,000+ professionals, with 25% of graduates landing impactful roles within six months at places like Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and the UK AI Security Institute. Entry point is the free, self-paced 2-hour "The Future of AI" course with no application required, followed by longer courses, grants, and in-person programs.

structured.duration: 2 hours (intro course); longer courses and week+ in-person programs

name: Google DeepMind: AGI Safety Short Course
current_details: A free, self-paced introductory course on AGI safety from Google DeepMind's safety research team, consisting of ~75 minutes of short recorded talks and exercises plus an accompanying slide deck and exercise workbook. It covers the path to superhuman capabilities, risks from deliberate planning and instrumental subgoals, how misaligned goals arise (specification gaming vs. goal misgeneralization), DeepMind's technical alignment approach (amplified oversight, robust training & monitoring, security & control, interpretability, safer design patterns, alignment stress tests), and its governance approach including frontier safety practices and dangerous capability evaluations. Aimed at students, researchers and professionals who want an accessible one-hour introduction to AI alignment.

name: MATS Slack #opportunities
current_details: Contract work, facilitation gigs, paper reviews, and collaboration opportunities from the MATS community.

name: Outsider's Roadmap to AI Safety (LessWrong)
current_details: A comprehensive guide published in July 2025 for professionals transitioning into AI safety research from technical backgrounds such as software engineering, physics, or data science. Covers three critical domains: interpretability research (reverse-engineering AI systems to understand their inner workings), alignment research (ensuring AI systems remain beneficial and share human values), and AI control & governance (technical policy for advanced systems). Written by someone actively making the transition, synthesizing insights from Neel Nanda's mechanistic interpretability resources, 80,000 Hours career research, and the broader alignment community, with practical advice on evolving roles (the shift from separate research engineers/scientists toward 'full-stack researchers'), required skills, and pathways for newcomers to contribute meaningfully to the field.

name: Anthropic Fellows Program
current_details: The Anthropic Fellows Program funds and mentors engineers and researchers to work on high-priority AI safety questions — scalable oversight, adversarial robustness, AI control, model organisms, mechanistic interpretability, AI security, and model welfare. Fellows work 4 months on empirical research with an Anthropic mentor, receiving a weekly stipend of $3,850 USD (£2,310 GBP / $4,300 CAD) plus ~$15K/month in compute funding. No PhD, prior ML experience, or published papers required; over 80% of first-cohort fellows produced papers and over 40% joined Anthropic full-time.

name: CAIS AI & Society Fellowship
current_details: A fully-funded, three-month in-person fellowship at CAIS in San Francisco for scholars in economics, law, international relations, and adjacent disciplines to pursue self-directed research on AI's societal impacts. Fellows receive a $25,000 stipend plus covered travel and daily lunch and dinner, and take part in guest speaker events, workshops, and a closing research presentation. Open to professors, PhD/JD holders or students, and researchers with equivalent experience; no prior AI research required.

name: CBAI Summer Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Rolling — Expression of Interest open for Spring 2026
current_details: CBAI's Research Fellowship is an intensive, fully-funded ten-week program in Cambridge, Massachusetts for researchers advancing careers in technical AI safety, AI governance, or technical governance. Fellows receive an $8,000 stipend, housing for non-local participants, meals, 24/7 Harvard Square workspace, up to $10,000 in compute credits, and weekly 1-2 hour mentorship from researchers at Harvard, MIT, Google DeepMind, UK AISI, CNAS and others. Open to undergraduates, master's and PhD students, postdocs, and early-career professionals (18+; OPT/CPT accepted but no visa sponsorship), with an extension program of up to 4 months available.

name: ERA Fellowship (Cambridge)
current_deadline: Closed — Winter 2027 cycle runs Jan 18 – Mar 26, 2027
current_details: The ERA:AI Fellowship is a 10-week intensive research programme in Cambridge, UK for people working on technical AI safety, AI governance, and technical AI governance. Fellows receive a competitive stipend, meals during working hours, covered transport, visas and lodging, dedicated research management, and a generous compute budget. The programme pairs each fellow with expert mentors from government, academia and industry and hosts 30+ events across the cohort.

name: Global AI Safety Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed — final deadline was 31 December 2024; expressions of interest accepted for the second iteration
current_details: Impact Academy's Global AI Safety Fellowship is a fully funded research program placing exceptional STEM talent with leading AI safety organisations including CHAI (UC Berkeley), Conjecture, FAR.AI, and the UK AI Safety Institute. Fellows work full-time for up to 6 months (or longer) and receive up to $30,000, plus an optional fully-funded AI safety bootcamp, mentorship, 1:1 coaching, and visa/logistics support. Applicants worldwide with demonstrated ML/deep learning knowledge, programming experience, and scholastic excellence are sought; a cohort of 10–20 fellows is selected via a two-phase, 4–6 week process.

structured.location: In-person preferred (US or UK partner orgs); hybrid/remote possible
structured.program_dates: Offers from March 2025 onwards; flexible start

name: Iliad Intensive / Fellowship
current_details: Iliad develops AI safety as a theoretical and experimental science through research, training, and fieldbuilding, incubating technical research organizations (AIXI Labs, Principia, Stormglass, XOR Labs) and running two training programs. The Iliad Intensive is a 4-week taught course in foundational AI alignment for researchers and technical practitioners with strong mathematical backgrounds, run monthly at venues including Lighthaven, LISA, and Mox. The Iliad Fellowship is a 3-month mentored research program for researchers developing work in mathematical and theoretical AI safety.

structured.stipend: Intensive: $5K travel-and-housing allowance; Fellowship: $18K travel-and-housing funding
structured.program_dates: Next Intensive: Nov 2–27, 2026 (LISA). Oct 5–30, 2026 (Mox) applications already closed; Fall Fellowship Sep 7–Dec 4, 2026 closed

name: MATS (ML Alignment Theory Scholars)
current_details: MATS is an independent research fellowship that connects talented researchers with top mentors in AI alignment, transparency, and security. Fellows conduct research for 12 weeks at offices in Berkeley, CA and London, UK, with the opportunity to apply for an additional 6–12 month funded extension. The program also runs a MATS Residency for long-horizon AI safety research, and mentor applications are currently open for the Winter and Summer 2027 cohorts.

name: AE Studio — AI Alignment Research Grants
current_details: The AI Alignment Foundation (formerly AE Studio) provides research funding plus dedicated engineering teams to accelerate high-risk, high-reward AI alignment research beyond interpretability, evals, and control. It targets alignment researchers with ideas their current institutional funding won't cover, as well as technical experts from other fields (cognitive neuroscience, mathematics, physics) whose perspectives could open new directions. Engineering teams can execute on proposals with as little as one hour per week of the researcher's time, and applicants are asked to describe a first experiment a good engineering team could run in 1–2 weeks.

structured.location: Marina Del Rey, CA (remote applications welcome)

name: Pivotal Research Fellowship
current_details: A 15-week in-person AI safety research fellowship in London (18 January – 30 April 2027) hosted at the London Initiative for Safe AI (LISA), with weekly 1-on-1 expert mentorship, dedicated research managers, workshops, and speaker sessions. Fellows receive a £6,000–£8,000 stipend (Senior Fellows with a PhD or strong track record get £8,000) plus travel, £2,400 housing for non-London fellows, weekday meals, and compute. Open to anyone 18 or older committed to making AI go well, regardless of academic background; applications involve a written form, video interview, mentor work task, and final interview.

name: Second Look Research (UChicago XLab)
current_details: Second Look Research is a project of the Existential Risk Lab (XLab) at the University of Chicago that produces open source replications of load-bearing empirical results in AI safety. The site hosts a Replications Fellowship for researchers who want to independently verify and validate influential findings, alongside published replication work and a form for community members to request specific replications.

name: SPAR
current_deadline: Fall 2026 closed — Spring 2027 applications open around December 2026
current_details: SPAR is a 3-month, part-time, remote research fellowship (run by Kairos) pairing aspiring AI safety, security and policy researchers with 250+ experienced mentors. Mentees commit 5–40 hours/week, produce real research that has reached ICML, ICLR and NeurIPS, and present at a virtual Demo Day with $7,000 in prizes plus a career fair featuring METR, Redwood Research, GovAI and MATS. Open to undergraduates, graduate students and professionals with technical or policy backgrounds; no prior research experience required.

structured.program_dates: Fall 2026 round (mentor applications June 26 – July 26, 2026; decisions July 27, 2026)

name: Coefficient Giving — Transition Grants
current_deadline: Closed – program transferred to BlueDot Impact (September 4, 2026)
current_details: Coefficient Giving's Career Development and Transition Funding provided grants to individuals at any career stage seeking to build career capital for work reducing global catastrophic risks, with particular interest in AI safety and global catastrophic biological risks. It supported graduate study, unpaid internships, independent study, career transition and exploration periods, postdocs, professional certifications, and sabbaticals, and was open to applicants in any country with no minimum or maximum number of grants. The program was handed over to BlueDot Impact on September 4, 2026 — prospective applicants should now apply through BlueDot's career transition and rapid grants programs, while existing grantees can still reach Coefficient Giving at careerdevelopmentfunding@coefficientgiving.org.

structured.location: Open to applicants in any country

name: Coefficient Giving — Technical AI Safety RFP
current_details: Coefficient Giving's (formerly Open Philanthropy) request for proposals for technical AI safety research spanning 21 research areas across five clusters: adversarial machine learning, sophisticated misbehavior in LLMs, model transparency, trust from first principles, and alternative approaches to mitigating AI risks. The fund expected to deploy roughly $40M over 5 months, with grants ranging from small API-credit requests to seed funding for new research organizations. Applications were submitted via an expression of interest form; the EOI window has now closed.

name: Foresight Institute AI Nodes
current_details: Foresight Institute's AI for Science & Safety Nodes offer grant funding, office space, community, and access to private local compute clusters at physical hubs in San Francisco and Berlin, plus a community xNode in Cape Town with the Cape Institute for Safe AI. The current RFP spans three calls: I. Local Compute, II. Coordination and accountability, and III. AI-first science (Bio, Neuro, Nano). Grants typically range from $30,000 to $100,000 (larger amounts possible), with strong priority given to applicants who will be active, in-person contributors at the Nodes; review takes roughly three months after the deadline.

name: Long-Term Future Fund (LTFF)
current_deadline: Closed - replaced by Transformative AI Fund
current_details: The Long-Term Future Fund (LTFF) has been permanently closed by EA Funds and replaced by the new Transformative AI Fund. The LTFF previously made early-stage grants (typically $10k–$150k, rarely above $300k) to individuals and organizations reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI, covering technical research, policy analysis, forecasting, advocacy, and field-building. A legacy LTFF page remains online but no longer accepts applications or donations — prospective applicants and donors should use the Transformative AI Fund instead.

name: Manifund Regranting
current_details: Manifund's AI Safety Regranting program gives expert regrantors independent budgets of $100K–$350K to fund AI safety projects they identify through their networks or via Manifund's open call. Because a single regrantor owns each budget rather than a committee, grants can be approved in days rather than months, and example grants have ranged from $11K to $200K. Manifund's 501c3 fiscal sponsorship lets regrantors fund individuals, unregistered projects, and (pending diligence) for-profit organizations, with all grants published publicly.

name: Meridian Cambridge — Research Accelerator Week
current_details: An intensive 6-day programme in Cambridge, UK (18–23 May 2026) that helps technical AI safety researchers move into funded independent research via a dedicated Coefficient Giving funding pathway. Participants form teams with 30+ researchers, submit an EOI, and leave with a completed grant proposal, plus fiscal sponsorship through Meridian and automatic consideration for a 3-12 month Visiting Researcher Programme residency. Workspace, accommodation, meals, visa support and travel reimbursement (up to £200 UK, £400 Europe, £700 international) are covered; the previous cohort secured over $1M in funding.

structured.stipend: Funding via Coefficient Giving grants; travel reimbursed up to £700

name: Schmidt Sciences — Trustworthy AI RFP
current_details: Schmidt Sciences' funding opportunities page lists its current open calls; the organization proactively seeks grant opportunities and does not accept unsolicited proposals. As of this check, no Trustworthy AI RFP (AI & Advanced Computing) call is listed — the only active calls are climate-related: Decarbonization Modeling of Urban Mobility and the Built Environment (DEVI) and Virtual Institute for the Carbon Cycle (VICC-2). Interested researchers can subscribe to the AI & Advanced Computing newsletter to be notified when a new AI call opens.

name: Schmidt Sciences — Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World
current_deadline: Closed — deadline was August 9, 2026 11:59 PM AoE
current_details: A joint funding call from Schmidt Sciences, Google DeepMind, ARIA, the Cooperative AI Foundation, and Google.org for foundational research on safety in multi-principal, multi-agent AI ecosystems. Two funding tiers were offered — Tier 1 up to $300,000 and Tier 2 $300,000–$1,000,000 — for 1–2 year projects across four clusters: sandboxes and testbeds, the science of agent networks, strengthening agent infrastructure, and multi-agent oversight and control. Decisions were expected in Autumn 2026; the call was open globally to individual researchers, teams, institutions, and multi-institution collaborations.

structured.program_dates: Applications opened Jun 11, 2026; closed Aug 9, 2026; decisions Autumn 2026

name: Survival & Flourishing Fund (SFF)
current_deadline: Closed — Main Round: April 22, 2026; Theme Rounds: June 10 / June 24 / July 8, 2026
current_details: The Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF) ran its 2026 S-Process Grant Round with $20–40MM+ in total funding across multiple rounds and tracks. The Main Round distributed $14–28MM via the Main Track ($10–20MM), Freedom Track ($2–4MM), and Fairness Track ($2–4MM), with recommendations announced in September 2026. Three new Theme Rounds — Climate Change, Animal Welfare, and Human Self-Enhancement & Empowerment — each offer $2–4MM, with recommendations due November 2026; late applications remain eligible for Speculation Grants and the next announced round.

structured.program_dates: Main Round recs September 2026; Theme Round recs November 2026

name: UK AISI Alignment Project
current_deadline: Closed - unlikely to run in 2026; check aisi.gov.uk/grants for future programs
current_details: The Alignment Project is a global fund launched in 2025 by an international coalition including UK AISI, CAISI, CIFAR, Australia's AI Safety Institute, OpenAI, Microsoft, AWS, Anthropic, Schmidt Sciences and others. It offers grants of £50,000 to £1,000,000 to researchers across disciplines — from computer science to cognitive science — plus dedicated cloud compute and API credits, potential venture investment, and support from AISI's Alignment team. Round 1 awarded over £27 million across more than 60 projects.

name: 5050 AI (Fifty Years)
current_details: 5050 AI is a 13-week free accelerator from Fifty Years helping AI researchers turn their work into startups focused on AI safety and alignment, with no equity and no fees. Mentors include Wojciech Zaremba (OpenAI co-founder), Emmett Shear, Ross Girshick, Dileep George, and Ronnie Chatterji, with cohorts in SF/Boston and London (in partnership with the UK's ARIA). 340+ alumni have launched 78 companies with a 95% seed raise success rate.

name: Catalyze Impact
current_details: Catalyze Impact is a 501(c)(3) non-profit incubator for AI safety, security, and resilience organizations, offering highly customized 1-on-1 support on direction & strategy, co-founder matching, mentorship from an expert network, and access to a seed funding network of grantmakers and investors, plus a stipend so founders can work full-time. Founders also join private office hours and Q&As with figures such as Jaime Sevilla (Epoch AI), Chris Akin (Apollo Research), and Eric Ho (Goodfire). The program has incubated ~15 organizations to date, with the majority raising 6 or 7 figures, spanning AI control, governance, and hardware security.

name: Halcyon Futures
current_details: Halcyon Futures is a nonprofit incubator and venture fund backing exceptional founders, operators, and researchers building in AI safety, biosecurity, and AI security (cybersecurity). It offers career transition grants up to $500K, nonprofit seed grants up to $1M (often wired within days), and venture investments of $1M+, alongside incubation, co-founder matching, network introductions to frontier labs and funders, and multi-day founder retreats. Its portfolio spans 25+ launched organizations that have raised $400M+ in follow-on funding and 150 supported career transitions.

structured.stipend: Grants up to $500K (career transition), up to $1M (nonprofit seed), $1M+ investments

name: ImpactOps
current_details: Impact Ops is an operations consultancy providing hands-on specialist support to high-impact organizations across AI safety, global health and development, animal welfare, and climate change. Services span finance (budgets to bookkeeping), recruitment, entity setup and fiscal-sponsor spin-outs, donor/grantee due diligence, operational audits, and systems implementation. Past clients include the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, BlueDot Impact, Foresight Institute, Forecasting Research Institute, Longview Philanthropy, Giving What We Can, Condor Initiative, Impact Academy, and Arkose.

name: Rethink Priorities Special Projects
current_details: Rethink Priorities' Special Projects Program provides fiscal sponsorship and comprehensive operational support — finance administration, accounting, recruitment, hiring via US/UK entities or an international Employer of Record, visa sponsorship, fundraising coordination, and event planning — so high-impact initiatives can launch and scale quickly. Fees for new projects are typically around 14% of project costs, varying with needs, complexity, and scale. Through end of 2025 the team had received 195 expressions of interest, supported 15 projects, expended $19.7M in direct costs, onboarded 114 sponsee staff, and completed 32 successful US/UK visa applications.

structured.location: Remote / US & UK legal entities, international hiring via Employer of Record

name: Seldon Lab
current_details: Seldon Lab is an AI security and safety startup accelerator focused exclusively on world-scale AGI deployment questions, investing in and hands-on building with founders working on existential security technologies. Beyond capital and mentorship, the team publishes research, builds systems, and deploys cyber-physical infrastructure, with network guests including Geoff Ralston, Emmett Shear, and Josh Achiam. Batch #1 companies collectively raised $10M+ with exits to xAI and Anthropic; Batch #2's Demo Day was held Apr 20, 2026.

name: WorkStream
current_details: WorkStream Nonprofit (High Impact Alliance, a 501c3) provides operations consulting, embedded implementation support, and advisory services to help nonprofits boost impact by 30% or more on the same budget. Its flagship six-month Operations Accelerator cohort brings together six growth-stage organizations to build sustainable systems, strategic planning skills, and workflow optimization, with applications accepted on a rolling basis. Additional offerings include a Grant Readiness Course, Operations Health Check, fiscal sponsorship and GRIP programs, plus free monthly webinars on budgeting, compliance, hiring, workflow, and fundraising.

name: 80,000 Hours Job Board
current_details: The 80,000 Hours Job Board is a continuously updated, handpicked collection of high-impact roles addressing the world's most pressing problems, including AI safety, AI policy, and existential risk reduction. Users can search and filter by salary, location, and role type, view hiring organisations, get personalised matches based on their background, save or hide listings, and subscribe to daily or weekly job alerts. Free 1-1 career advice and extensive career research (career guide, AI careers, list of top skills) are available alongside the board.

name: AISafety.com Jobs
current_details: AISafety.com Jobs is a continuously updated board currently listing 535 open roles across AI safety research, policy, engineering, operations, security and communications. Recent postings include positions at Google DeepMind, Anthropic, FAR AI, Safe AI Forum, SASH, Lucid Computing, EY, Carnegie Mellon SEI, NYU and MIT FutureTech, with salaries ranging from roughly $50,000 to $600,000. Roles span entry-level internships to senior leadership, many remote or based in the San Francisco Bay Area, New York, London, Washington DC, Amsterdam and Singapore, and many do not require technical skills.

structured.location: Global — SF Bay Area, New York, London, Washington DC, Amsterdam, Singapore, Pittsburgh, Boston, Remote

name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
current_details: The Center for AI Safety (CAIS) is a San Francisco-based AI safety non-profit working to reduce societal-scale risks from artificial intelligence through research, field-building, and advocacy. Its careers page currently lists no specific open roles, but invites interested candidates to email hiring@safe.ai with questions, and researchers can submit a collaboration form to work with CAIS.

name: FAR AI Careers
current_details: FAR AI's careers landing page invites applicants to join a team working to make advanced AI systems safe and beneficial, spanning research on trustworthy and secure AI, events convening global AI leaders, and field-building programs. The page is a general overview with no specific job listings, deadlines, compensation, or location details shown; openings are linked from elsewhere on the site and typically hired on a rolling basis.

name: MATS Alumni Hiring Database
current_details: A signup form to create an account for the MATS Alumni Hiring Database, which connects alumni of the MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars) Program with organizations hiring in AI safety. Registration requires only a full name, email, and agreement to the MATS Privacy Policy. This resource is exclusively for MATS program alumni.

name: MATS Careers (Staff Hiring)
current_deadline: Sep 27, 2026 (Program Manager for Mentor Selection, Program Coordinator, Impact Analyst); Oct 1, 2026 (Research Manager for Jan 2027 start); rolling for other roles
current_details: MATS is hiring across multiple staff roles to support its AI safety research program, including General Counsel (Berkeley), Research Manager (Berkeley, London, DC — apply by Oct 1 for a January 2027 start, then rolling), (Senior) Program Manager, Mentor Selection (Berkeley), Program Coordinator, Main Program (Berkeley), and Impact Analyst (Berkeley/London/Remote). Additional openings include Community Manager, Head of Finance, Executive Assistant (Berkeley), Executive Business Partner (London), and Operations Generalist (Berkeley). Candidates who don't match a listed role can submit a general Expression of Interest form.

name: What AI Safety Orgs Want in a Hire
current_details: Blog post from 80,000 Hours (published September 23rd, 2025) sharing survey results from 38 leaders of top AI safety organisations on what they look for in hires. Key takeaways: 1–3 years of relevant experience is often enough for many non-technical-research roles; most-recommended upskilling routes are BlueDot courses, the Talos Fellowship, MATS, GovAI fellowships, Cambridge ERA:AI, and Pivotal Research; hardest-to-fill profiles are chiefs of staff, policy professionals, Mandarin speakers, and European citizens with AI context. It emphasises publishing your work publicly and networking at events, and points to the 80,000 Hours job board with 300+ AI safety roles.

name: Apollo Research
current_details: Apollo Research is hiring across technical research, policy, and AI security product teams focused on frontier model alignment, scheming, deception, AI control, and loss-of-control risks. Most staff are based in London or San Francisco with regular office attendance, and benefits include competitive salary and equity, pension/401(k) matching, unlimited PTO, private medical insurance, 6 months paid parental leave, visa sponsorship and relocation support. The hiring process runs through a screening call, a 2-2.5 hour take-home task, role-specific interviews, and a final leadership interview, with successful candidates typically starting within 3 months of applying; no internships are offered.

name: Beneficial AI Foundation
current_details: The Beneficial AI Foundation (founded by Max Tegmark) is hiring for fully remote roles focused on keeping AI beneficial. Open positions include AI Safety Research Scientist (starting at $35–$75/hour) and Research Engineer (starting at $30–$70/hour), with pay depending on experience, track record, and demonstrated potential. Both roles are open to applicants remote from anywhere with no stated application deadline.

name: Forethought
current_details: Forethought Research is a non-profit researching how to navigate rapid AI progress and the transition to superintelligent AI, covering AI-driven social change, AI-enabled coups, governance, and long-run strategy. They currently accept two expressions of interest — a general researcher EOI and one focused on extreme power concentration — with no application deadline. Roles are based in Oxford or Berkeley (remote negotiable, UK/US visa sponsorship usually available), with 33 days annual leave, a £5k/yr professional development budget, 14 weeks full-pay parental leave, and a pension with 2x employer match up to £10k/yr.

name: Goodfire
current_details: Goodfire is an AI interpretability startup hiring agentic, mission-driven people to help build the future of understanding AI systems, including its Silico product line for LLMs, life sciences, and robotics/vision. All roles are full-time, in person five days a week at their San Francisco (Telegraph Hill) office. Open roles are listed on the careers page and can be filtered by team.

name: Gray Swan AI
current_details: Gray Swan AI is hiring across AI security research, adversarial evaluation, and red-teaming, including ML Engineer roles, with work that has directly informed the safety evaluations of frontier models such as Claude, GPT, and Gemini. Benefits include 28 days of holidays and PTO, 401(k) with up to 4% matching, flexible work arrangements, visa sponsorship, professional development support, medical/dental/vision coverage, catered lunches at the Pittsburgh office, and 100% paid parental leave with up to 14 weeks of paid birthing leave. Open roles are listed on the careers page and accepted on a rolling basis.

name: LawZero
current_details: LawZero is a non-profit AI safety lab in Montreal led by Yoshua Bengio, building non-agentic, safe-by-design AI to accelerate scientific discovery and provide oversight of agentic AI systems. Its Greenhouse board currently lists 15 openings across research, engineering, and operations in Montreal and Berlin, including Director of Evaluations, Machine Learning Manager, Mathematical Scientist for AI Safety Research, ML Research Scientist (probabilistic inference), Senior Distributed ML Engineer, Senior Data Platform Engineer, Platform Engineer, Technical Recruiter, and a Communications Specialist. A Talent Community sign-up is also available for future opportunities.

name: METR (formerly ARC Evals)
current_details: METR (formerly ARC Evals) is a research nonprofit conducting empirical research to measure AI capabilities, autonomy, and catastrophic risk, with work underpinning evaluation standards (STREAM, AEF-1) and frontier safety policies. Open roles in Berkeley, CA include Member of Technical Staff, Evaluation Execution ($328K–$578K, on-site), Member of Technical Staff, Security Engineering ($328K–$578K, hybrid), Task Development Engineer ($260K–$385K), System Administrator ($260K–$471K), Member of Technical Staff, Embedded Assessments ($402K–$687K), Member of Technical Staff, Cyberforensics ($402K–$578K), Chief Information Security Officer ($492K–$578K), and General Counsel ($328K–$402K). Benefits include unlimited PTO, medical/dental/vision, wellness ($1,500/yr), mental health ($6,000/yr), and professional development ($5,250/yr); a General Expression of Interest option is also available.

name: MIRI TGT Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - register interest for future cohorts
current_details: MIRI's Technical Governance Team runs a small research fellowship where fellows work on scoped projects at the intersection of technical and political AI governance, such as hardware verification, chip monitoring, and international agreement design. The program is 8 weeks at 40 hours/week with a $1,200/week stipend ($9,600 total), remote-by-default with an in-person kickoff week in Berkeley, CA (flights and housing provided). A main goal is identifying full-time hires; strong applicants have research or policy experience and care deeply about existential risk, and visas cannot be sponsored.

structured.location: Remote with 1-week kickoff in Berkeley, CA
structured.program_dates: An 8-week period between Feb 2, 2026 and Aug 31, 2026

name: Redwood Research
current_details: Redwood Research is hiring full-time Member of Technical Staff researchers in Berkeley, California to work on AI safety topics such as AI control, alignment faking, and safety cases. Candidates need machine learning and software engineering skills, strong communication, and a deep interest in mitigating AI risk. Compensation ranges from $350,000 to $850,000 per year depending on experience, and the team aims to respond to applicants within 2 weeks.

name: SAIF (Safe AI Forum)
current_details: SAIF (Safe AI Forum) fosters international collaboration on AI safety and currently lists three open roles: (Senior) Researcher – Misuse Risks to own and grow SAIF's work on extreme misuse risks from frontier AI and build the technical consensus enabling international coordination, General Counsel to own the Legal function and act as a strategic partner weighing legal risk against mission and operational reality, and Executive Business Partner to help run the organisation at higher capacity as it grows. They also welcome expressions of interest from talented individuals passionate about their mission even when no current opening fits.

name: Simplex
current_details: Simplex is an AI safety research organization founded in 2024 by Paul Riechers and Adam Shai, building a science of intelligence through computational mechanics and interpretability — including work on belief state geometry, constrained belief updating, in-context learning, and factored representations in transformers. They are currently hiring Research Scientists and Senior Research Scientists in the Bay Area (Emeryville, CA, at the Astera Institute) and Research Scientists in London. Recent output includes ICML and NeurIPS papers on how transformers learn factored representations and encode Bayesian belief geometry.

name: Transluce
current_details: Transluce is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit research lab in San Francisco building the public tech stack for scalable oversight of AI, including the Docent platform for understanding AI behaviors, activation oracles, scaling laws for exact string elicitation, and independent model evaluations (e.g. their mental health evaluation). The site carries a 'Join Us' link to external hiring listings but the main page lists no specific roles, compensation, or application windows. Recent output as of September 2026 includes essays on embedded evaluations and trillion-parameter activation oracle research.

name: WhiteBox Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Cohort 2 ended May 18, 2025 — expression of interest open for future cohorts
current_details: WhiteBox Research runs a 15-week AI interpretability and safety fellowship aimed at developing researchers in or near Southeast Asia, with an in-person track in Quezon City, Philippines and a virtual track for residents of South, Southeast, or East Asia. Fellows learn to train and interpret models like GPT-2 using ARENA-based exercises and gain research experience through two hackathons. The program is free (normally $3,000 USD), pays a $200 USD completion reward, and requires a minimum of 15 hours/week.

structured.stipend: $200 USD completion reward (program free, valued at $3,000 USD)
structured.location: Openspace Katipunan, Quezon City, Philippines (in-person) or virtual for South/Southeast/East Asia

name: 80K Hours: Top US Policy Masters Programs
current_details: A curated Airtable directory from 80,000 Hours listing 12 top US master's programs in national security, international affairs, and public policy, nearly all based in Washington, DC. Entries include Georgetown's Security Studies Program and MPP, RAND School's 9-month Master of National Security Policy and Master of Technology Policy, Johns Hopkins SAIS MAIR, George Mason's MS Biodefense, GWU's Security Policy Studies, American University, University of Maryland, and Texas A&M's Bush School DC campus. Each record covers tuition, duration, class times, GRE/GPA expectations, concentrations, start dates and application deadlines, with programs ranging from 9 months to 2 years and many offering part-time or evening options for working professionals.

structured.location: Washington, DC (some Santa Monica, CA options)

name: aisafety.com/funding
current_details: A continuously maintained directory of 56 AI safety funders — grant programs, funds, regranting platforms, and fiscal sponsors — spanning technical research, governance, field-building, journalism, and career transitions. Entries range from micro-grants ($10K from Leo Gao's Experimental Microgranting Program, BlueDot Rapid Grants) to large-scale philanthropy (Coefficient Giving's Project Tailwind at $200K–$200M, Mercor's $5M AI Safety Fund, OpenAI Foundation's $25B commitment). Each listing is tagged with its application status, with many open on a rolling basis and others currently not accepting applications.

structured.location: Global (incl. San Francisco, Berlin, UK, US)

name: Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship
current_details: The Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship supports PhD students and early-career researchers working on multi-agent cooperation and AI safety; the 2026 cohort of 14 fellows was selected from 240 applications (a 35% increase over the 2025 inaugural cohort). Fellows receive annual budgets for conferences, compute, wellbeing, and productivity, plus travel funding for CAIF events and access to collaboration with CAIF researchers and partner organisations. CAIF Scholars, ranked in the top 1% of applicants, additionally receive top-up funding of up to $40,000 per year for living expenses for up to 3 years.

structured.stipend: Up to $40,000/year (CAIF Scholars) plus annual conference, compute, wellbeing and productivity budgets

name: Cooperative AI Research Fellowship (Cape Town)
current_details: A full-time 3-month research fellowship in Cape Town, South Africa for researchers from diverse backgrounds to pursue AI safety work from a cooperative AI perspective, covering multi-agent safety, AI for human cooperation, mitigating gradual disempowerment, and wildcard projects. Fellows receive a $3,000/month stipend, a private room in a group house, flights to and from Cape Town, office space with workday meals, and a compute budget, plus mentorship from researchers at Google DeepMind, Oxford, and MIT. The 2026 cohort (31 January – 30 April 2026) of 10 fellows has concluded and research posters are now published.

name: FLI AI Safety PhD Advisor Directory
current_details: A directory of faculty members and AI researchers working on AI existential safety at universities worldwide, spanning roughly 60+ faculty and 114+ AI researchers at institutions including Oxford, Cambridge, UC Berkeley, Stanford, MIT, Princeton and CMU who are open to advising students on AI safety research. It is designed as a resource for finding a faculty mentor when applying for the Vitalik Buterin postdoctoral and PhD fellowships; awarded fellows receive automatic community membership. Professors and researchers can separately apply for community membership on a rolling basis to access funding leads, travel support, workshops and networking events.

name: Schmidt Sciences AI2050
current_details: AI2050 is a philanthropic initiative of Schmidt Sciences, co-chaired by Eric Schmidt and James Manyika, that supports exceptional researchers worldwide working on the key opportunities and hard problems critical to ensuring AI benefits society by 2050. Fellows are selected as Early Career or Senior Fellows through a nomination-only process and join an interdisciplinary research community. In November 2025 Schmidt Sciences announced $18M in new awards to researchers, following an earlier $10M commitment to AI safety research.

name: Vitalik Buterin PhD Fellowship (FLI)
current_details: The Vitalik Buterin PhD Fellowship in AI Existential Safety, run by FLI in partnership with the Beneficial AI Foundation, supports incoming and existing PhD students pursuing AI existential safety research. Fellows receive tuition and fees for 5 years, a $40,000 annual stipend (at US, UK and Canadian universities), a $10,000 research fund for travel and computing, and reimbursement of application fees for up to 5 PhD programs if short-listed. FLI has paused the program and will not accept applications in fall 2026 while it reassesses the program's direction, with no timeline announced.

name: AI Policy Leadership Network (APLN)
current_details: APLN is a part-time program organized by the Foundation for American Innovation, CNAS, and the Horizon Institute for Public Service that convenes experienced AI policy professionals — 6-25 years of experience including 4+ years in AI policy-relevant organizations across government, think tanks, military/intelligence, and industry. The 2026 cohort runs mid-March through late July 2026, with monthly evening off-the-record discussions in Washington, DC and one multi-day learning trip to the San Francisco Bay Area in April 2026. All program expenses including trip travel and accommodations are covered, but no stipend is provided and there is no homework or job placement.

structured.location: Washington, DC (with learning trip to San Francisco Bay Area)

name: Americans for Responsible Innovation
current_details: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) is a bipartisan AI policy nonprofit in Washington, DC advocating for a thoughtful, proactive framework for AI policy that safeguards Americans while preserving U.S. competitiveness. Its careers page lists open roles as they become available and currently shows no specific positions posted. ARI also runs a non-employee referral bonus of $3,000 for Director/VP-level hires and $1,500 for all other roles, paid after the referred hire completes 30 days of employment.

name: Career Accelerator (Horizon)
current_details: Horizon's Career Accelerator is a 9-month, part-time, remote program designed to launch careers in AI and technology policy. Participants access a modular mix of mentorship, dedicated training, application coaching, networking, exclusive opportunity listings, and a peer Slack community, with a time commitment of at most 5 hours per week during the optional training period. Participants can also apply for up to $100,000 in flexible funding for unpaid internships, upskilling, conferences, and career transitions; applicants range from students and recent graduates to mid-career professionals pivoting into AI policy.

name: CNAS Nye Internship
current_deadline: Rolling — target start dates October 2026 through April 2027
current_details: The Joseph S. Nye, Jr. National Security Internship and Mentoring Program at CNAS places interns directly with research programs or business departments including Communications, Design, Development, Defense, Energy, Economics, and Security, Indo-Pacific Security, Middle East Security, National Security Human Capital, Technology and National Security, and Transatlantic Security. Internships are full-time (40 hrs/week) for a six-month term, in person in Washington, DC, with a $1,900/month living stipend plus a $75/month transportation stipend. Applicants must be able to relocate to or already live in the DC area, and CNAS asks that application materials not be generated or revised with AI tools.

structured.program_dates: Target start dates: Design October 2026; Development October 2026; Communications November 2026; Defense March 2027; Energy, Economics, and Security April 2027

name: CSET Summer Internship (Georgetown)
current_details: A 10-week summer internship at Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), where interns conduct research on emerging technologies — AI, cybersecurity, AI workforce, and biotechnology — and their national security implications. Designed specifically for students from Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and other Minority-Serving Institutions (MSIs), the program is cost-free to interns: a competitive hourly wage plus living stipend, paid housing at Georgetown's intern housing (55 H St NW, downtown DC), and travel covered. Interns receive one-on-one mentorship, workshops, and finish by publishing a CSET blog post and presenting their findings.

structured.stipend: Competitive hourly wage + living stipend; housing and travel paid
structured.location: Washington, DC (Georgetown Capitol Campus, 500 1st St NW, Suite 700)

name: GovAI Summer Fellowship
current_details: GovAI runs a three-month Summer Fellowship in the UK (with parallel Winter and DC editions) on either a Research or Applied track, pairing fellows with a research manager to produce an ambitious AI governance project. Applications are accepted from anywhere in the world, and fellows receive career support and coaching alongside their 3-month placement. As of this listing, no fellowship application round is open — the opportunities page currently advertises only staff roles (Research Manager, Talent Program Manager, Hiring Specialist/Associate, Entrepreneur-in-Residence).

name: Horizon Fellowship
current_details: Fully-funded fellowship placing early-career and experienced professionals in Washington, DC policy roles focused on AI, biotechnology, and other emerging technologies. Fellows are placed at executive branch agencies, congressional offices, think tanks, or national laboratories for 1-year renewable terms (up to 2 years), or 6-month renewable terms for junior think tank fellows. For the 2027 cohort, base salaries are $78K/year (junior fellows), $130K/year (fellows), and $190K+/year (senior fellows), plus a $17K/year benefits-equivalent stipend, $3K professional development stipend, and up to $3K relocation assistance; applicants must be authorized to work in the US and willing to live in the DC area.

structured.duration: Up to 2 years (1-year renewable terms; 6-month terms for junior think tank fellows)

name: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship
current_details: The IAPS AI Policy Fellowship is a fully funded, 3-month program (Spring 2027 cohort) for professionals from varied backgrounds seeking to build practical AI governance policy skills, with Research and Applied tracks. Fellows receive $18K and Senior Fellows $24K stipends, plus an extra $3K for those on the D.C. or London track, with travel and accommodation support. All fellows must attend a 2-week in-person kickoff in Washington, D.C. (February 22 – March 5, 2027), then continue in D.C., London, or remotely with an expert mentor.

name: Longitude DC Intensive
current_details: A fully funded eight-day AI policy program in Washington, DC for people with a technical AI safety background who want to explore how their expertise could contribute to the AI policy ecosystem. 15 participants spend October 5–14, 2026 in talks, hands-on workshops, and networking with DC policy organizations, covering US government and AI policy foundations, policy career mapping, and post-program support (intros, advising) for moving into governance roles. Participation is free, with DC housing, meals on program days, and US travel covered; applicants need an undergraduate degree, AI safety context, and must be US citizens or currently based in the US.

structured.stipend: Fully funded (tuition, housing, meals, US travel)

name: RAND CAST Fellows
current_deadline: Next quarterly review deadline: November 1, 2026 (response by December 1, 2026)
current_details: The RAND Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST) Fellowship develops policy analysts and implementors at the intersection of technology and security, with mentorship from RAND experts and research in AI Security, Technology Policy and Governance, or Biosecurity (the only areas considered as of December 2025). Fellowships typically start at 6 months and can be renewed up to 3 years, full- or part-time, based in Washington DC, San Francisco, Pittsburgh, remote in the US, or the UK. U.S. fellows receive $40,000–$200,000/year stipends for full-time work plus a monthly health/dental payment; candidates from undergraduate to mid-career are welcome but must be able to obtain a U.S. or U.K. security clearance, and current RAND staff are ineligible.

structured.stipend: $40K–$200K/year (full-time, US); UK compensation based on experience
structured.location: Washington DC, San Francisco, Pittsburgh, remote US, or UK

name: Tarbell AI Journalism Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed Jan. 7, 2026 (2026 cohort); 2027 cohort not yet announced
current_details: The Tarbell Fellowship is a one-year program for journalists covering artificial intelligence, combining a 10-week remote AI and journalism fundamentals course, a weeklong summit in the San Francisco Bay Area, and a nine-month placement at a major newsroom such as Bloomberg, the Guardian, MIT Technology Review, NBC News, The Verge, or TIME. Fellows receive stipends of $60,000–$80,000 depending on location, while Senior Fellows (five or more years of journalism or AI experience) receive $90,000–$110,000. The program is open to applicants worldwide, though some placements require the right to work in the U.K. or U.S.

structured.location: San Francisco Bay Area summit; newsroom placements in US/UK and globally
structured.program_dates: June 8, 2026 – May 31, 2027 (Fundamentals June 8–Aug 14, 2026; Summit Aug 17–21, 2026; placement Sept 2026–May 2027)

name: Andon Labs — Summer 2026 Role
current_details: Andon Labs is a Y Combinator W24 company (founded 2023) building autonomous organizations without humans in the loop. The company is based in San Francisco with a team of 11 people and is listed as Active. No job openings are currently posted on the YC platform.

name: ARC Visiting Researcher
current_deadline: Rolling — expression of interest form open
current_details: The Alignment Research Center hires year-round visiting researchers, appointments that typically run ~10 weeks with flexible duration and serve as the usual entry path before any permanent role. Most successful candidates have a strong theoretical background in math, physics, or computer science; empirical ML experience is a plus but not required. Formal researcher hiring was paused over the summer with plans to re-open in September, so candidates are directed to the expression of interest form in the meantime; ARC is also hiring a Chief of Staff and an Automation Lead.

name: CHAI Internship (UC Berkeley)
current_deadline: Applications for 2026 internships are now closed
current_details: Research internship at UC Berkeley's Center for Human-Compatible Artificial Intelligence (CHAI) for people interested in human-compatible AI research, requiring a background in machine learning, computer science, mathematics or related fields. Interns work on a project supervised by a CHAI mentor, typically producing first-author workshop papers, over 12–16 weeks with flexible start dates (usually beginning around May). Compensation is $5,000/month for in-person interns at UC Berkeley and $3,500/month for remote interns; international applicants are accepted.

name: CLR Summer Research Fellowship
current_details: The Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR) runs an annual two-month Summer Research Fellowship at its London office, focused on s-risks (risks of astronomical suffering), AI safety and long-term future research. Fellows are supervised by CLR researchers or external experts and receive a salary of £4,925/month plus professional development and health/wellbeing budgets, with visa sponsorship available for international applicants. The program typically runs between June and September and has served as a main pipeline into full-time CLR research roles.

structured.program_dates: Typically June–September (usually starts June or July)

name: Constellation Astra Fellowship
current_deadline: Expression of interest open — next cohort dates TBD
current_details: Astra is Constellation's flagship 5-month, fully funded, in-person fellowship at its Berkeley research center, pairing emerging AI safety talent with senior mentors across an Empirical Research stream and a Strategy & Governance stream. Fellows receive a $8,400/month stipend, up to ~$15K/month in compute budget for empirical researchers, visa support, workspace, and dedicated research management and career support. Over 80% of the first cohort now work full-time in AI safety at organizations such as Redwood Research, METR, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, CAISI, and the UK AI Security Institute.

structured.program_dates: Program starts Jan 5 – ends Mar 31; optional extension Mar 31 – Jun 30

name: DeepMind Student Researcher
current_deadline: Rolling — see Google Careers for open listings
current_details: Google DeepMind's Student Researcher Program is a paid in-person internship placing students enrolled in Bachelor's, Master's or PhD programs alongside leading AI researchers across Google DeepMind, Google Research and other Google AI teams. Placements run 12–24 weeks with a minimum commitment of four days per week at a Google office. Applications are organized by degree level (BS, MS, PhD) and location, and a single application is considered for all relevant positions across Google's AI teams.

structured.location: In-person at a Google office (various locations)

name: LASR Labs — Summer 2026
current_deadline: Not yet announced — express interest for the June–September 2027 cohort
current_details: LASR Labs is a 13-week technical AI safety research programme in London where participants work in teams of 3-4 with an experienced supervisor to take a project from proposal to publication. Participants receive a £15,000 stipend plus food, office space, and travel, working in person from the London Initiative for Safe AI. Alumni have gone on to UK AISI, Apollo Research, OpenAI, Geodesic Research and Coefficient Giving, and LASR papers have been accepted at NeurIPS, ICLR and ICML — including three NeurIPS 2025 main conference papers and an ICML 2025 workshop best paper award.

name: OpenAI Emerging Talent
current_details: OpenAI's Emerging Talent hub gathers early-career pathways into the company: internships, a research residency, and full-time roles in research, applied engineering, and product for people with 0–3 years of experience. It's aimed at recent graduates and self-taught learners who want to work on building safe, beneficial AI, with openings listed continuously on the OpenAI careers board. Prospective applicants can also join the Emerging Talent Community for networking, virtual Q&As, and community events, and consult the OpenAI Interview Guide.

name: Tilde Research
current_details: Tilde Research is a mechanistic interpretability lab (backed by Khosla Ventures) currently listing 3 open technical roles: ML Researcher, ML Engineer, and Kernel Engineer. Each position is available as either an internship or full-time role and is based on-site in San Francisco. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis via the Ashby job board.

name: Virtue AI
current_details: Virtue AI is an AI security and compliance platform founded by Bo Li and Dawn Song. The company offers positions across research, engineering, operations, marketing, and sales in San Francisco, but currently has no open positions listed on their job board.

name: Coefficient Giving — Project Tailwind
current_details: Project Tailwind is Coefficient Giving's call for founders to launch ambitious new AI safety organisations, funded across three tiers: pre-seed $200K–$2M, seed $2M–$20M, and scale $20M–$200M, typically covering 18–36 months of runway. Applicants can pitch their own idea or pick from Coefficient's published list of unsolved problems (e.g. training fault injections, AI decision-making tools, alignment moonshots, a frontier capabilities observatory). Pre-seed applications do not require an existing legal entity, and non-US teams and public-benefit for-profits are eligible.

name: Thinking Machines Lab — Safety Research Grants
current_details: Thinking Machines Lab is offering Tinker grants of up to $50,000 in API/compute credits for safety research on open-weight models, following the release of their Inkling and Inkling-Small open-weight models. Priority research directions include making models safer to open (differential defense/offense capability, hazardous-data classifiers, tamper-resistant safety training), understanding alignment failure modes (emergent misalignment, reward hacking and oversight gaming), and measuring and forecasting risk (worst-case and marginal risk estimation). The list of directions is explicitly non-exhaustive and any safety project that could be accelerated by additional Tinker credits is welcome.

name: IFP — The Launch Sequence RFP
current_details: IFP's Launch Sequence RFP was a rolling call for short (200–400 word) project pitches to accelerate science, strengthen security, or adapt institutions in anticipation of advanced AI. Selected authors received a $10,000 honorarium, help turning the pitch into a full project plan, introductions to philanthropic funders, and support from an advisory panel including Wojciech Zaremba, Tom Kalil, Matt Clifford, Kathleen Fisher, and George Church; $1,000 bounties were offered for successful referrals and published new ideas.

name: Paradigm 3 Research Fund
current_details: Paradigm 3's research fund supports work on measuring and forecasting AI capabilities and impacts, alongside its in-house research. Current grantees are studying AI externalities (e.g. time lost to authentication challenges), decomposing benchmark gains into cheating/memorization/shallow vs. OOD generalization, and the desirability and mechanics of slowing AI progress. They invite proposals on topics including centaur evals, 'guardian angel' user-aligned models, the virtue-vs-rules alignment divide, generalization gaps, scaling and 'unhobbling', automated science, compute growth, and recursive self-improvement — prospective grantees email hi@paradigm3.org.

name: grantmaking.ai Launch Round
current_details: grantmaking.ai's inaugural Launch Round offered $1M total for work reducing x-risk from AI, with grants of $5k–$50k per applicant. A single short application created a public project page and funding ask visible to every funder on the platform, reviewed by grantmakers including Gavin Leech, Ryan Kidd, and Marcus Abramovitch. Applications for this round have closed, though projects can still be listed with a public funding ask.

structured.program_dates: Applications opened June 29; deadline July 13; decisions by July 31

name: Falcon Fund (Manifund)
current_details: The Falcon Fund is a Manifund-hosted animal welfare fund led by regrantor Marcus Abramovitch, making rapid (under 1 week) early-stage grants of $25K–$150K, with a particular focus on the intersection of animal welfare and transformative AI. Priority areas include animal harm benchmarks, animal welfare constitutions for frontier models, industry watchdog work, and raising animal welfare salience inside AI labs. The fund has raised $379,932 toward a $2M goal and grantmaking is largely active/outbound, though contact is open via marcus.s.abramovitch@gmail.com.

name: MARS — Cambridge AI Safety Hub
current_deadline: Applications closed May 10, 2026 — EOI open for December 2026 cohort
current_details: MARS is a part-time, hybrid AI safety research programme from the Cambridge AI Safety Hub that pairs teams of 2–4 mentees with experienced mentors to produce publishable technical and governance research. The cohort includes 2–4 weeks of prework, a 1-week in-person kick-off, and 8–10 weeks of remote part-time work at 8–15+ hours/week. It is unpaid but free to attend, with travel, accommodation, meals, a $2k+ compute budget, Claude Max, and research management provided.

structured.stipend: Unpaid — costs covered (travel, accommodation, meals, $2k+ compute)
structured.program_dates: Jul – Oct 2026 (in-person Jul 13–26, 2026); next cohort December 2026

name: TARA — Technical Alignment Research Accelerator
current_details: TARA (Technical Alignment Research Accelerator) is a free 14-week part-time technical AI safety program for talent across the Asia-Pacific region, based on the ARENA curriculum. Participants attend full-day Saturday in-person sessions plus 2-7 hours of independent study weekly, covering transformers, mechanistic interpretability, RL, and model evaluations, culminating in a 3-week research project. Round 2 2026 runs in 10 cities with ~194 participants; a refundable commitment bond (e.g. $200 AUD) applies.

structured.stipend: Free program (no stipend); refundable commitment bond $200 AUD / ₹3,000 INR / ¥12,000 JPY etc.
structured.location: APAC — Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Manila, Tokyo, Singapore, Taipei, Hong Kong, Delhi, Bangalore

name: AI Safety Camp
current_details: AI Safety Camp is a 3-month fully virtual research program (12th edition) in which participants form teams around preselected projects covering AI alignment, deconfusion research, and efforts to stop or pause harmful AI development. Project Lead applications are open now — leads need prior research or organizing experience and must commit at least 10h/week; team member applications open November 7, 2026 and close November 29, 2026. No stipends are currently available, apart from a few projects backed by matched donations.

name: Dovetail Research Fellowship
current_details: Dovetail is a research group working on foundational mathematics research aimed at understanding the nature of AI agents, with the mission of helping humanity safely navigate the creation of powerful AI systems. The group is funded in part by the Long-Term Future Fund (LTFF) and the Advanced Research + Invention Agency (ARIA), and its research agenda is published as a public wiki. The site includes a Jobs section, but the landing page lists no fellowship cohort dates or application details.

name: Generator Residency
current_deadline: Closed - check for next cycle (summer 2026 round closed April 27, 2026)
current_details: Generator is a 3-month residency in Berkeley run by Kairos and Constellation for AI safety generalists — agentic executors from technical, ops, policy, engineering, design or writing backgrounds — who pitch, build, and ship projects that strengthen AI safety ecosystem capacity and infrastructure. Residents receive a $6k/month stipend plus housing, travel, project budgets, Constellation office access and mentorship, with placement support into full-time AI safety roles afterward; selected residents can extend for another three months. The summer 2026 cohort (15–30 residents) ran June 15 – Aug 28, 2026; only expressions of interest for the next round are being collected now.

name: AIXI Labs Fellowship
current_details: Universal Algorithmic Intelligence (uaiasi.com) is a community hub for researchers working on Solomonoff induction, AIXI, and related mathematical foundations of intelligence, hosting regular online research meetings, a paper-discussion group, and an "Introduction to Universal Artificial Intelligence" reading group as an on-ramp for new students. It periodically runs fellowships for UAI/AI-safety research, with a recent post announcing fellowships awarded in September 2026. The site also publishes community blog posts on topics such as imitation learning, corrigibility, and the coding theorem.

name: Frame Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed — Cohort 2.0 applications closed August 5, 2026; express interest for next cycle
current_details: The Frame Fellowship is a 10-week accelerator in San Francisco for content creators building high-quality video content that educates the public about AI and its societal and economic implications. Fellows receive housing, meals, and a $10,000 stipend, plus mentorship from creators like Rob Miles, Drew Spartz, and Liron Shapira, with two tracks (Independent and Amplifier, the latter embedding with orgs such as MATS, Apart Research, and CAIS). Cohort 2.0 runs September 7 – November 15, 2026; applications are closed but an expression-of-interest form collects sign-ups for the next cycle.

name: Collective Intelligence Project Research Fellowship
current_details: The Collective Intelligence Project's pilot Research Fellowship supports 3 fellows for 6 months to conduct original research using CIP's proprietary datasets (Global Dialogues multi-country AI attitude surveys, Collective Generation deliberation data, and the Weval evaluation platform) at the intersection of AI, public values, and democratic governance. It is remote and non-residential at 5–10 hours/week with a fixed $9,000 stipend paid in three milestone-based tranches. Aimed primarily at late-stage PhD candidates and early-career postdocs in political science, computational social science, sociology, or CS/ML, though independent and international scholars are welcome.

name: Frontier AI Security Residency
current_deadline: Not yet announced — mailing list open for the 12 Oct – 4 Dec 2026 cohort
current_details: The Frontier AI Security Residency (FASR) is an 8-week, fully funded in-person research and engineering programme in Cambridge, UK, run by ERA in partnership with Heron and the Oxford Hardware AI Governance Lab. Residents work with mentors from leading AI hardware and cybersecurity teams on concrete projects in hardware-enabled verification, cybersecurity and policy, running 12 Oct – 4 Dec 2026. No formal application form is live yet — the site currently collects interest via its mailing list.

name: Heron AI Security Research Fellowship
current_details: Heron's AI Security Research Fellowship pairs experienced cybersecurity professionals (5+ years) with AI security field leaders on 10-12 collaborative research teams tackling projects in AI infrastructure security, technical AI governance, adversarial/model security, AI control and containment, and cyber evaluations. The program runs 3 months (September–November 2026) remote-first with coworking hubs in London, Tel Aviv and San Francisco, requiring 8-30 hours/week. It is unpaid, but teams receive $1,000+ in compute, Claude Code Team accounts, and up to $5K per team in conference travel support, with a guaranteed presentation at the AI Security Forum in Tel Aviv.

structured.stipend: Unpaid — $1,000+ compute credits per team, up to $5K/team conference travel support
structured.location: Remote-first; coworking in London, Tel Aviv & San Francisco

name: CBAI AIxBiosecurity Fellowship
current_deadline: Fall 2026 round closed (Sept 6, 2026); Spring cycle applications open late September 2026
current_details: The CBAI AIxBiosecurity Research Fellowship is a fully-funded 10-week research program in Harvard Square, Cambridge, MA, focused on AI-enabled biological risk — dangerous capability evaluations, safeguards and unlearning for bio-relevant models, biosurveillance, DNA synthesis screening, and AI governance. Fellows receive a $15,000 stipend, housing for relocators, free meals, 24/7 office access, weekly 1:1 mentorship from researchers at SecureBio, RAND, Harvard, Active Site, Protectome and LatchBio, plus ~$1,500/week in compute credits. It runs alongside the CBAI AI Safety Research Fellowship for a combined cohort of 40 fellows; students, recent grads, postdocs and experienced professionals (as Senior Fellows) are welcome.

name: AI Security Bootcamp — London
current_details: AI Security Bootcamp London is a 7-day intensive, fully funded program for experienced security professionals working on securing frontier AI systems, running Dec 6–12, 2026 in London. The curriculum spans threat modeling, adversarial attacks, LLM and infrastructure security, weight security, AI control, and hardware governance through lectures, demos, and hands-on red/blue team exercises. Tuition, meals, and accommodation are covered with need-based travel support; 20 participants are accepted and 5+ years of hands-on security experience is required (no prior AI/ML background needed).

structured.stipend: Fully funded (tuition, meals, accommodation; need-based travel support)

name: Frontier AI Security Training (FAST)
current_details: Frontier AI Security Training (FAST) is a 5-day fully funded, in-person intensive in Singapore for 20 experienced cybersecurity and machine learning practitioners, run by SASH. Participants learn to attack and defend frontier models and agents through hands-on labs covering AI control, open-weight security, and verification, finishing with career mapping, funding pathways, and one-to-one instructor sessions. It is not introductory — applicants need hands-on PyTorch experience (ML4Good/ARENA level) or deep technical security work.

name: FAS AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship
GovAI U.S. AI Policy Program
current_details: The GovAI U.S. AI Policy Program is a bipartisan, part-time, 12-week program for U.S. policy professionals in government and think tanks, building a technically-informed understanding of the AI policy landscape. It requires about 5 hours per week (3 hours reading plus 2 hours of evening synchronous sessions held in-person at GovAI's D.C. office near DuPont Circle or remotely), and is free of charge with dinner provided for in-person attendees. Eligible applicants include executive and legislative branch staff, fellows, interns, detailees, military and national lab personnel, and think tank researchers, with preference for those in the D.C. metro area.

name: Vista Institute for AI Policy
current_details: The Vista Institute for AI Policy (a fiscally sponsored project of Rethink Priorities) builds the academic field of AI law and policy and develops talent through part-time virtual courses, DC workshops, and a fellowship. Its 2026 virtual courses — National Security Law and AI (Aug 10–26), AI Agents and the Law Module 1 (Aug 19–Sep 4), and Module 2 (Sep 7–Oct 2) — have all begun or concluded. The AI Law and Policy Fellowship sponsors students and recent graduates for independent research or research-assistant placements, but has no public application: completing a Vista course is what makes you eligible to apply.

name: Singapore AI Safety Hub (SASH)
current_details: The Singapore AI Safety Hub (SASH) is a Singapore-based organisation bridging governments, academia and industry across East and West on trustworthy frontier AI, with applied technical governance research in verification mechanisms, frontier safety evaluations and agent governance. It runs the Singapore AI Safety Fellowship for researchers and the Frontier AI Security Training (FAST) Policy Lab for policymakers, plus public talks, private convenings and a co-working space in Singapore for AI governance and safety practitioners. The site also lists open roles, hiring globally.

name: Center for Technology & Statecraft
current_details: The Center for Technology & Statecraft (CTS) is a non-partisan AI policy research initiative based in Washington, DC, founded by former White House NSC and Commerce Department technology official Saif M. Khan. Its team of technologists, analysts, and former policymakers conducts technical, forward-looking research on AI's societal transition, US-China competition, semiconductor supply chains, export controls, and compute infrastructure. The site hosts a Careers page, but this homepage lists no specific internship or fellowship openings, application windows, or deadlines.

structured.location: Washington, DC (1225 Union St NE, Ste 800)

name: Secure AI Project
current_details: Secure AI Project is a San Francisco-based AI policy and safety advocacy organization that develops and advocates for pragmatic policies to reduce risks of severe harm from advanced AI. The site includes a Careers page and a list of bills the organization supports, but the homepage lists no specific internship or fellowship openings, application windows, or deadlines.

name: SAIGE Incubator — Safe AI Germany
current_deadline: Closed — Spring 2026 cohort deadline was March 22, 2026
current_details: The SAIGE Incubator is Safe AI Germany's national mentorship program pairing newcomers with expert mentors on AI safety projects across four tracks: Technical AI Safety, AI Governance & Policy, Technical AI Governance, and Communications & Field-Building. Mentees work in teams of 1–5 at 10–20 hours per week for roughly 3 months (April 27 – July 31, 2026, with an optional 3-month extension), alongside a tailored AI safety crash course, weekly mentor meetings, research skills workshops, a global speaker series, and career guidance. No prior AI safety experience is required; backgrounds in CS, maths, law, political science, psychology, economics, operations or field-building are welcome.

name: BlueDot Impact — Incubator Week
current_deadline: Cohort v6 runs November 2–6, 2026 — applications rolling
current_details: BlueDot Impact's Incubator Week is a 5-day, all-expenses-paid founder sprint in San Francisco where technically serious people working in AI safety, biosecurity, cyber, or other catastrophic-risk fields develop threat models, build interventions, and pitch on Friday for funding of up to $100k in grants. Past cohorts total 50 participants who have raised $7M+ in external funding, with alumni founding orgs like Exona Lab, 0Labs, Telluvian, and safely.bio. No polished idea is required — you just need to be ready to leave your current role and build; referrals earn $2,000 per accepted person.

structured.stipend: Up to $100k in grant funding; all expenses paid

name: Neolithic
current_details: Neolithic is a newly founded nonprofit startup in San Francisco building open-source, agentic tools and infrastructure to accelerate AI safety research, with projects spanning rogue-deployment datasets, evaluation-awareness mitigation, agent infrastructure, and automated reward hacking detection. It is funded to bring on its first two hires immediately, offering end-to-end project ownership and direct collaboration with researchers at leading AI safety organizations. It also invites safety researchers and orgs to request custom tooling, which Neolithic will build and maintain for free.

name: d_model
current_details: d_model is a fundamental AI research lab partnering with frontier labs to turn their models into capable interpretability and alignment researchers, building RL environments for open-ended interpretability tasks. The team publishes interpretability research on topics like concept-erasure algorithms discovered by LLM agents, how models represent nullability, and steering characters via interpretability. Career opportunities are handled through a general Hiring Interest Form rather than a formal application window.

name: Allelo
current_details: Allelo is a new AI safety research initiative (fiscally sponsored by Rethink Priorities) studying what propensities and character traits make AI agents safe to deploy in complex, multi-agent, sometimes adversarial real-world settings, with an initial focus on susceptibility to influence. It aims to produce concrete agent-design recommendations for frontier labs, regulators, and certification bodies. The team is currently hiring a full-time Senior Researcher at USD 120,000–150,000, location-flexible with London preferred, potentially convertible to a co-founder role.

name: RESI — Institute for Responsible Superintelligence
current_details: RESI (Institute for Responsible Superintelligence) is a nonprofit research institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts building the scientific foundations for superintelligence that is "safe by design," applying the cryptography playbook of precise definitions, constructions, composition, and impossibility results to AI safety. It was founded by Turing Award winner Shafi Goldwasser, cryptographer Vinod Vaikuntanathan, and former OpenAI Safety Systems researcher Adam Tauman Kalai, with a research team spanning computer science, mathematics, economics, law, and ethics. Work is organized into AI-assisted working groups (verification and delegation, modular architectures, incentives, cryptographic and legal mechanisms), with an active visitor program; topics and working group leaders are still to be announced.

name: Verified Mechanisms
