current_details: Verified Mechanisms is an independent, grant-funded research project (funded via Manifund) building a formally verified autoresearch pipeline for theoretical mechanistic interpretability, where multiple frontier LLM agents collaborate to generate theorems that are machine-checked in Lean 4. The pilot problem asks how many attention heads are needed to compute a Boolean function, and outputs include an open-source multi-agent orchestration harness and the xorformer theorem ledger repository. The team states it plans to onboard additional researchers over the coming months for multi-agent orchestration and mech interp work — there is no formal application form, but interested people can join the Discord or email hello@verifiedmechanisms.ai.

name: PauseAI — Vacancies
current_details: PauseAI's vacancies page currently lists no open positions, but the organisation welcomes spontaneous applications from people passionate about its mission to pause frontier AI development. Candidates can send a CV and brief cover letter to vacancies@pauseai.info; applications are kept on file and considered when paid roles next open, though a response is not guaranteed.

name: ML4Good Technical Bootcamp
current_deadline: Not yet announced — join notification list
current_details: ML4Good's Technical Programme is a free, residential AI safety bootcamp covering transformers from scratch, interpretability, RLHF, evaluations, technical governance, and a 2-day capstone project with mentorship. Food, accommodation and teaching are provided at no cost, travel may be reimbursed, and cohorts are organised regionally so participants come from the same area. It targets people with some coding experience (coding is ~25-30% of the curriculum) who are committed to contributing substantially to AI safety; alumni have gone on to MATS, SaferAI, UK AISI and the EU AI Office.

structured.stipend: Free to attend; food, accommodation and teaching covered, travel possibly reimbursed
structured.location: Rotating regional venues (recent: UK, Canada, Germany, South Africa, France, Singapore, Brazil, Italy, Colombia)
structured.program_dates: No upcoming cohorts announced; most recent was UK – September 2026

name: Successif
current_details: Successif offers free, expert-guided career development for experienced professionals transitioning into AI risk reduction work. Support includes personalized 1:1 career advising, resume and interview help, professional training workshops, introductions to AI safety organizations, and a peer community, alongside specialized programs such as an AI Policy Strategy Fellowship and a Women's Program. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis via the site's Apply form.

name: MIT AI Risk Initiative
current_details: The MIT AI Risk Initiative is an ongoing research project producing open data and frameworks for identifying, prioritizing, and managing AI risks. Its resources include the AI Risk Repository (a living taxonomy of AI risks, now at Version 4), an AI Incident Tracker, a governance database mapping global AI laws and policies to risk domains, an AI Risk Mitigation Database, and the AI Risk Navigator, an interactive tool that links all datasets through shared taxonomies. The site also publishes a blog with research updates, framework summaries, and project news, plus a newsletter.

name: ALIGN — AI Alignment Network
current_details: ALIGN (AI Alignment Network), a Japanese non-profit founded in September 2023, is recruiting volunteer staff across event operations, community management, PR/social media, research and writing, website maintenance, and organizational administration. Applicants are ideally able to commit 3–4+ hours per week, with basic admin/IT skills; English ability is a plus, and depending on fit and ALIGN's finances a paid role of roughly 1–2 days per week may be discussed. Selection is by application via the Contact form (with a short experience and motivation statement), followed by an online interview.

structured.stipend: Mostly volunteer; possible paid staff role (~1–2 days/week) depending on fit and funding

name: Vegas AI Security Forum
current_details: The Vegas AI Security Forum is an annual invite-based gathering (held alongside Black Hat/DEF CON week) convening experts in AI, cybersecurity, and national security to work on securing powerful AI models. The most recent edition, Vegas AI Security Forum '26, took place Aug 6, 2026 in Las Vegas and has concluded. The organizers' other events remain open: TLV '26 on Nov 22, 2026 in Israel and a DC Reading Group are both accepting applications.

name: ELLIS Institute Tübingen — AI Safety & Alignment Group
current_details: The AI Safety and Alignment Group at the ELLIS Institute Tübingen, led by Maksym Andriushchenko (EPFL postdoc and ELLIS Member), develops technical solutions to reduce risks from general-purpose AI models. Research focuses on alignment of autonomous LLM agents, rigorous AI evaluations, public communication about frontier model risks, and understanding how models generalize from training data. The group currently hosts four PhD students and interns in Tübingen, Germany; this is a group overview page with no specific application window listed — check the institute's Careers page for open PhD and internship positions.
